records.subject: relic_beast
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Relic Beast
evidence.species: Original relic-beast; cream fur, huge ears and amber eyes, tiny cracked horns, one fang, enormous curled tail
evidence.personality: Curious, stubborn, opportunistic, delighted by anything shiny.
evidence.backstory: A nameless den-scavenger whose chest Core woke when a buried vault rang beneath the Hideout. It has no famous bloodline or prophecy; it keeps surviving because it pokes everything that glows and runs faster than consequences.
evidence.silhouette: Huge ears + curled tail + tiny horns + glowing chest Core + satchel
evidence.palette: cream, charcoal, amber-gold Core, scavenged olive/brown gear
evidence.pose_notes: Balanced posture; weapon weight is the joke. Ears/tail react to anticipation and rewards.
evidence.future_passive: Scavenger's Instinct — first treasure interaction each encounter gains a tiny utility bonus, not raw mandatory power.
evidence.starter_pitch: Balanced, adaptable, and ready for any ridiculous weapon.

records.subject: emberhorn
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Emberhorn
evidence.species: Fox-dragon relic-beast with swept ember horns, compact muzzle, thick expressive tail
evidence.personality: Brave, cheeky, impatient, loot-obsessed; treats danger like a dare.
evidence.backstory: Emberhorn hatched in the soot vents beneath an abandoned smelter and learned that most locked doors open if hit hard enough. Its Core burns hotter near ancient metal, which it interprets as treasure saying hello.
evidence.silhouette: Swept horns + fox ears + flame-tail tuft + broad forearms + hot Core
evidence.palette: burnt orange, dark charcoal, brass, ember-red, white-hot highlights
evidence.pose_notes: Chest-forward confidence; strong anticipation crouch; attacks overcommit in a charming way.
evidence.future_passive: Hot Start — the first damaging hit after a brief lull gains a small fire-flavoured bonus.
evidence.starter_pitch: Bold, punchy and built for players who like obvious impact.

records.subject: mosskin
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Mosskin
evidence.species: Leaf-eared forest relic-beast with bark plates, mossy mantle and seedpod charms
evidence.personality: Patient, protective, dry sense of humour, secretly competitive.
evidence.backstory: Mosskin guarded a collapsed waystone shrine long after everyone forgot what the shrine was for. When treasure hunters finally arrived, Mosskin decided the safest place for the relics was apparently in its own backpack.
evidence.silhouette: Leaf mantle + low sturdy stance + bark shoulder plates + broad tail frond
evidence.palette: moss green, bark brown, pale fern, warm jade Core
evidence.pose_notes: Grounded stance, low center of gravity, defensive bracing and protective recovery.
evidence.future_passive: Rooted Nerve — the first heavy hit taken in an encounter grants a brief modest guard.
evidence.starter_pitch: Steady and forgiving without being slow or boring.

records.subject: moonkip
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Moonkip
evidence.species: Long-eared moonlit relic-beast with scarf streamers, compact paws and crescent markings
evidence.personality: Playful, smug, curious, steals snacks before valuables and denies both.
evidence.backstory: Moonkip grew up inside the roof maze of the old Archive, learning every shortcut and none of the rules. It can hear Relic locks click before they open and has been banned from three vaults it technically discovered.
evidence.silhouette: Long ears + trailing scarf + crescent cheek mark + narrow agile body
evidence.palette: midnight blue, moon-silver, pale cream, cyan-violet Core
evidence.pose_notes: Low crouches, lateral feints, springy recoveries, sharp eye-line toward target.
evidence.future_passive: Slipstep — periodic attack/reward interactions grant a tiny burst of tempo or avoidance.

records.subject: pebblewyrm
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Pebblewyrm
evidence.species: Chunky juvenile stone-wyrm with crystalline back plates, tiny wings and oversized paws
evidence.personality: Sweet, fearless, food-motivated, thinks every problem is pushable.
evidence.backstory: Pebblewyrm was found asleep inside a geode that miners mistook for treasure. It woke, ate the claim marker, and followed the nearest Lootling home. Nobody has successfully explained property law to it.
evidence.silhouette: Rock plates + crystal nubs + barrel body + tiny wings + massive paws
evidence.palette: slate, violet crystal, dusty lilac, bright amethyst Core
evidence.pose_notes: Strong squash/stretch; attacks begin compressed and end dramatically extended.
evidence.future_passive: Rolling Momentum — repeated successful hits slowly build a tiny impact bonus that resets when combat pauses.

records.subject: glimmerfin
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Glimmerfin
evidence.species: Axolotl-fin relic-beast with luminous frills, glossy eyes and floating droplet motes
evidence.personality: Bright, excitable, easily distracted by magical phenomena, compulsive note-taker.
evidence.backstory: Glimmerfin emerged from a flooded observatory carrying a staff twice its height and absolutely no explanation for how it learned to use it. Its Core hums in harmony with unstable Relic weather.
evidence.silhouette: External frills + round tail fin + luminous droplets + floating focus motes
evidence.palette: aqua, sky blue, coral-pink frills, pearly white, cyan Core
evidence.pose_notes: Staff/focus anticipation, floating droplets orbit during charge, elastic magical release.
evidence.future_passive: Resonance — first status application in an encounter gets a small utility amplification.
evidence.starter_pitch: Bright spell effects and expressive magical reactions.

records.subject: gloomlet
records.canonical_source: art/reference/docs/lootlings_master_catalog_v1.json
records.blocker: Historical design record only; current runtime/canon controls implementation

evidence.name: Gloomlet
evidence.species: Small shadow-bat/cat relic-beast with hood-like ears, winged mantle and lantern Core
evidence.personality: Quiet, dramatic, sarcastic, tries very hard to look mysterious while loving praise.
evidence.backstory: Gloomlet lived in the sealed ventilation shafts of Hoard Depths and became convinced it was the terrifying spirit of the vault. The first adventurer who offered it dried fruit ruined the legend permanently.
evidence.silhouette: Bat-cat ears + wing mantle + narrow tail + dangling lantern-like Core
evidence.palette: charcoal, black-plum, magenta-violet, pale eye glow
evidence.pose_notes: Low stalking posture, vanish-like compression, fast diagonal release, theatrical victory pose.
evidence.future_passive: Opportunist — modest bonus against already-weakened enemies.
evidence.starter_pitch: Sneaky, dramatic and built around sharp payoff.

evidence.foreground: Grass tufts, loose coins, cracked pots, dangling roots, occasional close parallax pillar edge.
evidence.palette: navy night, sandstone gold, teal moss, amber relic light
evidence.music: Curious adventure; warm pluck, light hand drum, distant bell, gentle relic shimmer.
evidence.loot_theme: scavenged starter gear, basic charms, practical weapons

dialogue: If it sparks, it's either valuable or educational.
That dent? Structural personality.
I can fix it. Define 'fix.'
Don't lick the blue metal. Again.

Legendary? Put it down gently and act like we meant to find it.

Your Stash is full. Congratulations on your problem.

records.subject: nym

evidence.name: Nym
evidence.visual: hooded small horned keeper; layered violet cloth, floating shard rosary, calm bright eyes
evidence.backstory: Nym listens to Relic Cores the way other people listen to weather. Nobody is sure whether the Cores answer.
dialogue: The Core is louder today.
Power remembers how you used it.
A bright relic is not necessarily a kind one.
You came back carrying more noise than you left with.
Shards don't make choices. You do.
The altar likes you. I remain undecided.
That Legendary is singing through the wall.
Breathe before you spend everything.
Some vaults open with keys. Others open with consequences.
If the Core flickers, step away. Politely.

records.subject: quillik

evidence.name: Quillik
evidence.visual: small feather-crested lizard/bird relic scholar; spectacles, scroll harness, ink-stained paws
evidence.backstory: Quillik started the Archive to record relic history and immediately became distracted cataloguing increasingly stupid weapon names.
dialogue: I filed that under 'bad ideas, successful.'
New trophy! Try not to make the next one medically interesting.
I need the exact name. 'Big purple thing' is not archival language.
Your kill count has become a formatting problem.
Secret achievements are secret. Stop asking.
The dragon entry now has a footnote: 'rude.'
I have three books about that weapon. None recommend swinging it indoors.
You discovered a variant! I discovered paperwork.
Please stop bleeding on the rare manuscripts.
History is mostly people opening things labelled DO NOT OPEN.
